name: copane
description: Shares your VS Code window with Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and other MCP agents: its integrated browser tabs and terminals, per window and per agent session, with you able to step in.

copane.sessionGraceSeconds.description: How long a disconnected agent session keeps its tabs and terminals before they are released. Lets an agent reconnect after a window reload.

enumDescriptions: Every tool.

The everyday tools only: browsing, reading and acting on pages, tabs, dialogs, hand-off to you, and terminals. Leaves out the dev and test extras (emulate, route, audit, check change, inspect, export test, profiles) and rarely used tools (hover, drag, upload file, downloads, session info), about a third of what the tool list costs.
copane.tools.profile.markdownDescription: Which tools agents get. Every tool's definition is part of every conversation, and some agents (GitHub Copilot, Codex) load all of them up front; VS Code allows 128 tools per request across all MCP servers. `core` keeps the everyday tools. Connected agents get the new list right away (their next request cannot reuse its prompt cache). `window_status` and `window_select` are always there.

copane.tools.disabled.markdownDescription: Tool names agents do not get, on top of `#copane.tools.profile#`, e.g. `["browser_route", "terminal_close"]`. A call to one is refused with a message saying it is turned off. Unknown names are ignored; `window_status` and `window_select` cannot be turned off.

copane.usageNotesInResults.markdownDescription: Give Copane's usage notes to GitHub Copilot sessions once, with their first tool result, because Copilot does not pass an MCP server's instructions to its model. Turn this off if you start Copilot with `--allow-all-mcp-server-instructions`: the notes would then arrive twice.

enumDescriptions: Ask before an agent session reads or controls a browser tab you opened (once per tab, or per site).
Let every agent session use browser tabs you opened without asking.
Never let agent sessions use browser tabs you opened; they work in their own tabs.
copane.browser.userTabs.description: Whether agent sessions may use integrated-browser tabs that you opened. Tabs an agent opened itself are always available to it.

copane.browser.leaseIdleSeconds.description: How long an agent session keeps control of a browser tab without acting in it. After that the tab's indicator disappears and another session may take control.

copane.browser.pageIndicator.description: Show a small indicator in the page (and a thin frame in the session's color) while an agent session controls a browser tab, with a button to take over.

enumDescriptions: When an agent session opens a site with an untrusted certificate, ask whether to proceed (once per host). Hosts in the trusted list proceed without asking.
Never proceed past certificate errors for agents. You can still proceed yourself on the browser's error page.
copane.browser.certificateErrors.description: What happens when a browser tab an agent session is driving hits a certificate error (self-signed, company authority, wrong host name).

copane.browser.trustedCertificateHosts.markdownDescription: Hosts whose certificate errors are accepted without asking in tabs an agent session is driving, for local and company servers with self-signed or internally issued certificates. Exact host names (`localhost`, `build.corp.example`) or `*.corp.example` for a domain and all its subdomains. Choosing **Always Trust** in the prompt adds a host here.

enumDescriptions: Ask once per agent session before keeping a file it downloaded.
Keep files agents download without asking; the status bar shows each one.
Never keep files agents download (they are deleted, and the agent is told why).
copane.browser.agentDownloads.markdownDescription: Whether files that agent sessions download in browser tabs are saved to `#copane.browser.downloadsFolder#`. Your own downloads are not affected: VS Code keeps asking you where to save them.

copane.browser.downloadsFolder.markdownDescription: Where files that agent sessions download are saved. Empty: a `Copane` folder in your Downloads folder. `~/...` is relative to your home folder, a relative path to the first workspace folder. A file never replaces an existing one: it gets a name like `report (1).csv`. In a remote window (WSL, SSH, containers) this folder is on the remote side, where the agent runs: the browser saves on your computer first and Copane copies the file over.

copane.browser.loginPrompts.markdownDescription: When a site or proxy asks for a login (HTTP authentication: Basic, Digest, NTLM) in a browser tab an agent session is driving, ask you for it in VS Code instead of letting the page fail. The agent never sees what you type. Logins are remembered until the window closes, or saved in VS Code's secret storage if you choose **Log In and Remember**; **Copane: Forget Saved Browser Logins** removes them. While a session drives a tab, every request of that tab passes through the bridge.

enumDescriptions: Tabs agent sessions open use the window's default login store, which your own tabs use too: agents are logged in wherever you are.

Every agent session opens its tabs in a private login profile of its own, which starts logged out; agents cannot open tabs in your default store. They can still use named profiles and, with your permission, tabs you opened.
copane.browser.agentLoginStore.markdownDescription: Which login store (cookies, local storage, cache) browser tabs of agent sessions use when neither the agent nor you chose a profile for them. A profile you choose for a session in the Sessions view, or one the agent names, comes first. Login profiles live in memory until VS Code quits; see **Copane: Open Browser Tab in Login Profile…**.

enumDescriptions: Ask once before adding the "copane" MCP server to the user configuration of Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot. Afterwards Copane keeps its own entry present and up to date (it re-adds it if something removes it) until you run "Copane: Turn Off".
Add and keep the "copane" MCP server in the user configuration of Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot without asking.
Never change agent configuration on its own; only report problems. Use "Copane: Turn On", "Copane: Turn Off" and "Copane: Check and Repair Setup".
copane.registration.mode.markdownDescription: How Copane makes its tools available to agents. It adds an MCP server named `copane` to the user configuration of Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`), Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`) and GitHub Copilot (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`), and never changes or removes a `copane` server it did not add.

copane.registration.claudeCode.markdownDescription: Register the `copane` MCP server with Claude Code (the `claude` CLI and the Claude Code VS Code extension).

copane.registration.codex.markdownDescription: Register the `copane` MCP server with Codex, when Codex is installed.

copane.registration.copilot.markdownDescription: Register the `copane` MCP server with GitHub Copilot (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, or `$COPILOT_HOME/mcp-config.json`), which the Copilot CLI and Copilot chat in VS Code read, when Copilot is installed.

enumDescriptions: Ask before an agent session reads or types in a terminal you opened (once per terminal and session).
Agent sessions may read and type in your terminals without asking.
Agent sessions never get access to your terminals (they still see that they exist).
copane.terminal.userTerminals.description: Whether agent sessions may read and type in terminals you opened yourself.

enumDescriptions: Keep the session's terminals open, so you can still read them; whatever runs in them keeps running.
Close the session's terminals that are at an idle prompt; keep those still running something (e.g. a dev server).
Close all of the session's terminals, stopping whatever runs in them.
copane.terminal.onSessionEnd.description: What happens to an agent session's terminals when the session ends (after the reconnect grace period).

copane.ui.favicons.markdownDescription: Show each site's icon on its browser tab rows in the Sessions and Agent Tabs views, instead of a generic globe or state icon. The icon is the one VS Code's browser already shows on the editor tab; Copane loads nothing for it. Icons over 32 KB, in other formats, or SVGs with scripts or outside references are not shown.

enumDescriptions: The first time you collapse a session's tabs while pinned tabs are not compact, ask whether to make them compact.
When collapsing a session's tabs, set `#workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing#` to `compact` in your user settings if it is not.
Never change `#workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing#`: collapsed tabs keep the size pinned tabs have.
copane.ui.collapsedTabSizing.markdownDescription: Copane collapses an agent session's browser tabs by pinning them at the left of the tab bar. They take little room only when `#workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing#` is `compact`, a setting that applies to all pinned tabs in VS Code, your own too. Whether Copane may set it.

copane.vscodeChat.serverDefinition.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Also offer the `copane` MCP server to VS Code's own chat and agent mode (GitHub Copilot chat) as a server this extension provides, which always connects to *this* window, instead of guessing the window from the working directory. Not yet verified with a signed-in Copilot. Together with the `mcp-config.json` entry (`#copane.registration.copilot#`), a Copilot chat session may list Copane twice or use the other entry; if it does, turn off one of the two: this setting, or the `mcp-config.json` entry with `copilot mcp disable copane` (which also turns Copane off for the Copilot CLI) and `#copane.registration.copilot#` off.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No agent is connected to this window yet.
Start Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot in this window, in its chat or in a terminal. Each session appears here with the browser tabs and terminals it uses, and you can pause it or step in at any time.

[Get Started](command:copane.openWalkthrough)
Two one-time steps: let agents use the integrated browser, and turn Copane on for Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot.
Already set up? [Show Status](command:copane.showStatus) explains why nothing is connected.

The integrated browser is not enabled for Copane, so agents can use terminals but no browser tabs.
[Enable Integrated Browser](command:copane.enableBrowser)
VS Code restarts once to turn it on.
This editor has no integrated browser that extensions can drive, so agents get the terminal tools here but no browser tabs.

No agent session is using a browser tab in this window.
Tabs that agents open or control are listed here in the color of their session. Click one to bring it to the front.

The integrated browser is not enabled, so agents cannot open or use browser tabs.
[Enable Integrated Browser](command:copane.enableBrowser)
This editor has no integrated browser that extensions can drive, so agents cannot open or use browser tabs here. Their terminals are in the Copane view.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Copane
walkthroughs.description: Let Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot work in this window's browser tabs and terminals, next to you.

steps.title: What Copane does
steps.description:
Copane gives Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and other MCP agents the VS Code window they run in: its integrated browser tabs and its terminals. You see every click and every command, and you can take over at any moment.
Two one-time steps follow: let agents use the integrated browser, and turn Copane on for your agents.

media.altText: A VS Code window with a browser tab and a terminal, both marked with the color and label of the agent session using them.

steps.title: Let agents use the integrated browser
steps.description:
VS Code's integrated browser is controlled through an API that is still marked proposed. VS Code allows it only for extensions named in its argv.json, and reads that file only when it starts.
[Enable Integrated Browser](command:copane.enableBrowser)
Copane adds one line to argv.json and keeps the rest. Then quit VS Code completely and start it again: reloading the window is not enough. Until then agents get the terminal tools.

media.altText: The line "enable-proposed-api": ["saka.copane"] in argv.json, and a restart of VS Code.

steps.title: Restart VS Code to turn the browser on
steps.description:
argv.json already lets Copane use the integrated browser, but VS Code reads it only when it starts, and this VS Code started before.
[Quit VS Code](command:workbench.action.quit)
Then start it again. This step is checked off once the browser is available.

media.altText: The line "enable-proposed-api": ["saka.copane"] in argv.json, and a restart of VS Code.

steps.title: Let agents use the integrated browser
steps.description:
This is a remote window (WSL, SSH or a container). Copane runs on the remote side, but the browser and its setting, argv.json, belong to VS Code on this computer. The button opens that file (as **Preferences: Configure Runtime Arguments** does) and adds the line; if it cannot, it copies the line for you to paste.
[Enable Integrated Browser](command:copane.enableBrowser)
Then quit VS Code on this computer completely and start it again.

media.altText: The line "enable-proposed-api": ["saka.copane"] in argv.json, and a restart of VS Code.

steps.title: No browser tabs in this editor
steps.description:
This editor has no integrated browser that extensions can drive (VS Code's proposed browser API), so there is nothing to enable: agents get Copane's terminal tools here, but no browser tabs. The browser tools need an editor that includes VS Code's integrated browser, such as Visual Studio Code 1.140 or newer.
[Show Status](command:copane.showStatus)

media.altText: A window whose browser area is empty because the editor has no integrated browser, and a terminal that agents still use.

steps.title: Turn Copane on for your agents
steps.description:
Copane adds an MCP server named copane to your user configuration of Claude Code (~/.claude.json), Codex (~/.codex/config.toml) and GitHub Copilot (~/.copilot/mcp-config.json, read by the Copilot CLI and by Copilot chat in VS Code), and keeps it current. Nothing else in those files changes.
[Turn On](command:copane.registerAgents)
In a remote window that is the configuration on the remote machine, where the agents run. **Turn Off** in the Copane view's ... menu removes it again.

media.altText: Claude Code and Codex connected to the copane MCP server, which connects them to this VS Code window.

steps.title: Install an agent
steps.description:
Copane gives its tools to agents that speak MCP. None of Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot was found on this machine (or they are turned off in Copane's settings). Install one of them, then turn Copane on for it.
[Find the Claude Code Extension](command:workbench.extensions.search?%22anthropic.claude-code%22)
[Turn On](command:copane.registerAgents)
Other MCP clients work too: run the server at ~/.copane/bin/mcp-server from them.

media.altText: Claude Code and Codex connected to the copane MCP server, which connects them to this VS Code window.

steps.title: Try it
steps.description:
Start a **new** Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot session in this window (sessions that were already running do not see Copane's tools) and give it this prompt:
“Use the copane tools: set your session title to "Copane tour", open https://example.com in a VS Code browser tab and tell me the page heading, then run node --version in a VS Code terminal and tell me what it printed.”
[Copy Prompt](command:copane.walkthrough.copyPrompt)
A browser tab opens on example.com and a terminal named after the session (Claude 1) runs the command, both marked in the session's color, and the session appears in the Copane view. Your agent may ask you to approve its tool calls.

media.altText: An agent's prompt, then a browser tab on example.com and a terminal running node --version, both labelled Claude 1.

steps.title: See and control agent sessions
steps.description:
Every agent session in this window is listed in the Copane view with its label, color, tabs and terminals. There, or in a browser tab's title bar, you can pause an agent and take over a tab, release it, interrupt or close a terminal, or end the session. The Agent Tabs view in the bottom panel lists the browser tabs agents use.
[Open the Copane View](command:copane.sessions.focus)
When something does not work, **Copane: Check and Repair Setup** fixes what it can, and **Copane: Show Status** explains the rest.

media.altText: The Copane view: session Claude 1 with its title, browser tab and terminal, and buttons to pause, release and end.
